title: Proposed Constitutional Amendment: To Require Voters to Present Photo Identification in Order to Vote
plain_english: This would write Ohio's photo-ID voting rule into the state constitution. Since 2023, state law (HB 458) already requires voters to show photo ID when voting in person. This amendment would make that rule much harder for a future legislature to change or repeal, since changing the constitution requires another statewide vote. It also sets ground rules for voters who don't vote in person and lists exactly which IDs count.
yes_means: The photo-ID requirement is added to the Ohio Constitution effective immediately. The in-person photo-ID requirement becomes changeable only by another constitutional amendment. The constitution fixes the list of acceptable IDs (unexpired Ohio driver license/state ID, U.S. passport/passport card, U.S. military ID, Ohio National Guard ID, VA ID). Voters not voting in person must provide an approved photo ID unless state law lets them use a signature plus at least one other unique identifier.
no_means: The constitution is unchanged and photo ID remains required only by current state law (HB 458), which the legislature can still change by a simple majority vote.
official_ballot_language: Proposed by Joint Resolution of the General Assembly. To enact Section 5 of Article V of the Constitution of the State of Ohio. A majority yes vote is required for the adoption of Section 5. This proposed amendment would: Require voters to present an approved form of government-issued photo identification in order to vote. Allow state law to provide for an alternative method of verifying a voter's identity for a voter who has a sincere religious objection to being photographed. Require that voters who do not vote in person provide an approved form of government-issued photo identification, unless the law authorizes those persons to vote by providing a signature and at least one other specified unique identifier. If approved, the amendment shall take effect immediately. SHALL THE AMENDMENT BE APPROVED? YES / NO
supporters_say: The official pro-amendment argument (authors: State Reps. Adam Bird and Heidi Workman, State Sens. Theresa Gavarone and Jane Timken) says: 'Requiring a photo ID helps verify a voter's identity and ensures that only legal votes are counted,' calling it a 'commonsense requirement' that 'will protect Ohio's elections.'
opponents_say: The official anti-amendment argument (authors: State Sen. Bill DeMora, State Reps. Desiree Tims and Terrence Upchurch) calls it a 'blatant political attack' on citizens' right to vote, arguing 'Photo Identification is already the law and this amendment locks in voter burden with no voter protections' and 'Voter impersonation is essentially nonexistent.'

title: Proposed Charter Amendment - City of Conneaut (Ban on Large Data Centers)
plain_english: Adds a new article to Conneaut's city charter banning the construction of large data centers, defined as facilities used mainly for digital data services with a power demand above 25 megawatts. Smaller computer facilities under that power threshold would not be affected. The ban would take effect on its own ('self-executing') without needing further city action.
yes_means: The city charter is amended to ban construction of data centers drawing more than 25 megawatts. Building (or preparing to build) such a data center anywhere in the city is prohibited.
no_means: The charter is unchanged; no ban is imposed. Data-center projects remain subject to existing zoning and permitting.
official_ballot_language: Shall the Charter of the City of Conneaut be amended to add Article XVI to read as follows: ARTICLE XVI CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES. Section XVI-1. Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center. (A) The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) 'construction' shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities. (C) 'data center' shall mean one or more buildings or facilities used primarily or exclusively for digital information services with an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty five (25) megawatts. (D) This Section is self-executing. Shall the proposed charter amendment be adopted? YES / NO
supporters_say: The petition drive was organized locally with support from the group Conserve Ohio. Petition signature collector Joel Specht said of the rumored project: 'We know there has been one in the works.' Organic farmer Julia Barton cited heavy water use and excessive noise, saying the development 'has the potential to be a detriment to the things that sustain us.'
opponents_say: UNVERIFIED - no published statements from local opponents of the Conneaut ban were found in available sources.
context: Developer M2 Development Solutions has been studying a data center at the Conneaut East Industrial Park, and the city council rejected a proposed data-center moratorium in 2026. Nine Ohio communities have matching 25-megawatt ban petitions, and 18 Ohio communities total are voting on data-center measures Nov. 3.
